label: Week 1
goal: Learn the core LEGO Technic pieces and use them to build strong structures, rolling cars, and safe launch mechanisms.

days.activity: Project: learn how LEGO Technic beams and pins connect, then build the tallest freestanding tower that can stand on its own for 10 seconds.
days.assignment: Build and test a tall Technic tower. Record what made it stable and what you changed after your first test.
days.coachNotes: Open Lesson Deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%201/lesson1_lego_technic_assets_version.html. Concepts: beams, pins, stability, wide bases. Measure each tower after it stands independently for 10 seconds.
beginLessonQuestions: What do you already know about Tallest Tower?
What is one thing your team should test carefully today?
What will make this build successful?

days.activity: Project: engineer a Technic bridge across a gap and test how triangles, supports, and bracing help it hold more weight.
days.assignment: Build a bridge across the test gap. Record where it bent first and what reinforcement helped most.
days.coachNotes: Open Lesson Deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%202/lesson2_bridge_assets_version.html. Concepts: tension, compression, supports, triangular bracing. Test with the same gap and add weight gradually.
beginLessonQuestions: What do you already know about Strongest Bridge?
What is one thing your team should test carefully today?
What will make this build successful?

days.activity: Project: build a car powered only by air from a balloon, then tune the frame, wheels, and balloon direction for the farthest roll.
days.assignment: Build and test a balloon car. Record your best distance and one design change that made it roll farther.
days.coachNotes: Open Lesson Deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%203/lesson3_spike_prime_assets_version.html. Concepts: axles, wheel alignment, friction, air propulsion. Have balloons and straws ready; measure from the same start line.
beginLessonQuestions: What do you already know about Balloon-Powered Car?
What is one thing your team should test carefully today?
What will make this build successful?

days.activity: Project: build a safe Technic catapult that uses a lever and stored energy to launch a soft target toward a marked zone.
days.assignment: Build and test a catapult. Record how you balanced launch distance, accuracy, and safety.
days.coachNotes: Open Lesson Deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%204/lesson4_catapult_assets_version.html. Concepts: lever, fulcrum, stored energy, accuracy. Use only soft projectiles and aim away from people.
beginLessonQuestions: What do you already know about Catapult?
What is one thing your team should test carefully today?
What will make this build successful?

label: Week 2
goal: Use stored energy, pulleys, axles, balance, gravity, and fair testing to build machines that move, lift, spin, and roll.

days.activity: Project: build a rubber-band-powered car and test how stored elastic energy turns into distance and speed.
days.assignment: Build a rubber band car. Record your best distance and what happened when you changed winds, wheels, or weight.
days.coachNotes: Open Lesson Deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%205/lesson5_rubber_band_car.html. Concepts: stored elastic energy, axle drive, traction, speed versus distance. Keep winding rules consistent.
beginLessonQuestions: What do you already know about Rubber Band Car?
What is one thing your team should test carefully today?
What will make this build successful?

days.activity: Project: build an elevator or lift that raises a small cargo load smoothly and safely.
days.assignment: Build a lift. Record the height reached, the load carried, and the design change that made lifting smoother.
days.coachNotes: Open Lesson Deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%206/lesson6_elevator_lift.html. Concepts: pulleys, winches, guides, balanced loads. Use a small cargo box and measure lift height.
beginLessonQuestions: What do you already know about Elevator / Lift?
What is one thing your team should test carefully today?
What will make this build successful?

days.activity: Project: build a Ferris wheel that rotates smoothly, stays balanced, and carries small passenger cars.
days.assignment: Build a Ferris wheel. Record how you balanced the wheel and what helped it spin smoothly.
days.coachNotes: Open Lesson Deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%207/lesson7_ferris_wheel.html. Concepts: center axle, balance, rotation, crank motion. Encourage symmetric weight around the wheel.

days.activity: Project: design a marble run that uses gravity, slope, barriers, and supports to create the longest reliable ride.
